predecessors.name: Ethiopian Empire
predecessors.text: the colony of Italian Eritrea, formed from territory around Massawa ceded in the Treaty of Wuchale (1889)

successors.name: British Africa
successors.text: Tripolitania (February 1943) and Cyrenaica (November 1942) under 'British military administration' (1943-1951), and Eritrea and Italian Somaliland occupied by British forces in 1941

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: the Fezzan, occupied by the Free French in 1943

successors.name: Ethiopia
successors.text: Ethiopia, restored to Haile Selassie after the Italian collapse of 1941

ledger.x: 1890: the Majeerteen sultanate is an Italian protectorate.
1890: the Hobyo sultanate is an Italian protectorate.
1890: Italy founds the colony of Eritrea at Massawa.
1891: Italian forces occupy Adale on the Benadir coast.
1893: Merca, Mogadishu, Barawa and Warsheekh occupied.
1894: an Anglo-Italian protocol fixes Italy's sphere in Somalia.
17 July 1894: Italy annexes Kassala to Italian Eritrea.
1895: Italian troops march into Tigray.
April 1895: Baratieri occupies Adigrat and Adwa and annexes Tigray.
1896 or later: Italy leaves Kassala.
1896: Italy loses Tigray.
1896: Menelik wins at Adwa and Italy recognises Ethiopia.
1897: Asmara becomes the capital of Eritrea.
1911: Italy declares war on the Ottoman Empire and lands in Libya.
1912: the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war on 18 October.
18 October 1912: the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war.
October 1912: the interior stays out of Italian hands.
August 1914: the Italian advance to Ghat puts the Fezzan briefly under Italian suzerainty.
November 1914: the Fezzan is lost.
1917: the Treaty of Acroma.
1918: Tripolitanian rebels found a republic.
1922: Italian forces occupy Misrata.
26 January 1923: the Cyrenaica war begins.
1924: the northern half of the rebel contest ends.
1923-1924: Italy retakes Tripolitania north of the line.
1924: the southern half of the rebel contest begins.
1924: the Sirtica campaign.
1925: Britain cedes Jubaland (Oltre Giuba) and Italy merges it into Italian Somaliland.
1 October 1925: the protectorate of Hobyo ends.
1 October 1925: Italy occupies Hobyo and deposes the sultan.
October 1925: the Majeerteen protectorate turns into war.
October 1925: the Italians land at Alula and Hafun and fight the Majeerteen.
1925: Egypt cedes the Jarabub oasis (and, on paper, the Kufra district) to Italian Libya.
Late 1927: the Majeerteen are beaten. the Italians could not fully capture Majeerteenia 'until late 1927', after the fighting at Iskushuban sent Hersi Boqor and his staff into the Ogaden.
End of 1927: Italy annexes the Majeerteen sultanate after the Campaign of the Sultanates (1925-1927).
Late 1928: the southern half of the rebel contest ends.
Late 1928: Italy takes Ghibla.
1930: Italian forces conquer the Fezzan.
1931: Graziani seizes Kufra.
1932: the Cyrenaican resistance is crushed.
January 1932: Cyrenaica beyond the coastal towns passes under Italian control.
1934: the Sarra Triangle is turned over to Italy.
1936: Italy takes Addis Ababa on 5 May and Mussolini annexes Ethiopia on 9 May.
1939: the coastal provinces of Libya are incorporated into Italy.
July 1940: the Italian offensive on the Sudanese border begins.
July 1940: Moyale.
1940: Italy annexes British Somaliland.
13-18 September 1940: the Italian invasion of Egypt.
11 December 1940: 'the Italians were defeated at Sidi Barrani', the first battle of Operation Compass; the page does not date the last Italian post on Egyptian soil.
December 1940: Operation Compass.
1941: Moyale returns to the British.
18 January 1941: the Italians leave Kassala.
February 1941: Operation Compass takes Cyrenaica.
1941: British forces occupy Italian Somaliland.
March-April 1941: the Axis counter-offensive retakes Cyrenaica.
8 April 1941: British forces recapture British Somaliland.
1941: Eritrea falls.
1941: Addis Ababa falls on 6 April.
1941: the last Italian stand in East Africa ends at Gondar.
December 1941: Operation Crusader.
January 1942: Operation Theseus.
June 1942: Gazala and Tobruk.
November 1942: the Eighth Army wins the swings.
November 1942: Cyrenaica is lost for good (Tobruk 13 November, Benghazi 20 November).
January 1943: the Free French take the Fezzan.
February 1943: Italian rule in Africa ends in Libya.

wars.name: First Italo-Ethiopian War
wars.outcome: Ethiopian victory: 'Sovereignty of Ethiopia confirmed; border with Italian Eritrea delineated' (treaty of October 1896).

wars.name: Italo-Turkish War
wars.outcome: Italian victory: the Treaty of Ouchy (18 October 1912) gave Italy Libya.

wars.name: Pacification of Libya
wars.outcome: Italian victory: Tripolitania north of the Ghadames-Mizda-Beni Ulid line (1923-1924), the Sirtica (1924), Ghibla (late 1928), Fezzan (1930) and Kufra (1931) taken; Omar Mukhtar captured September 1931; the campaign declared ended January 1932.

wars.name: Campaign of the Sultanates
wars.outcome: Italian conquest: Hobyo occupied from 1 October 1925 (dubat columns under Colonel Di Bello) and the Majeerteen not fully taken 'until late 1927'; both sultanates annexed to Italian Somalia.

wars.name: Second Italo-Ethiopian War
wars.outcome: Italian victory: Addis Ababa captured 5 May 1936, Ethiopia annexed 9 May 1936 and merged with Eritrea and Somalia into Italian East Africa on 1 June 1936.

wars.name: East African campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory: Kassala and Moyale taken in July 1940 and British Somaliland in August; the Italians left Kassala on 18 January 1941; Italian Somaliland fell on 26 February, Keren on 27 March, Asmara on 1 April, Addis Ababa on 6 April, Massawa on 8 April…

wars.name: North African campaign (Western Desert campaign)
wars.outcome: Allied victory: the Italian invasion of Egypt (13-18 September 1940) failed at Sidi Barrani (11 December); Operation Compass took Cyrenaica by 9 February 1941, the Axis retook it in April 1941, lost it in Operation Crusader (December 1941), retook it in…

certainty.note: Eritrea's frontier is sharp after the Treaty of Addis Ababa (October 1896, 'delineated the borders of Eritrea'); the Somali spheres (Anglo-Italian protocol of 1894) and protectorates are approximate.
Libya's desert frontiers are approximate; Italian control of the interior 'remained limited until the late 1920s'; the Egyptian cession of Jarabub (1925) is a treaty line.
Ethiopia's frontiers were those of the old empire and the colonial lines, all approximate in the desert and highland borderlands.
